notes.1745: Title Implementation of AI to Robot Dynamics; printed Lecture Number 55 and footer 1.
notes.1746: Contents roadmap: dynamics revision, FFNN, forward dynamics pipeline, MLP inverse dynamics on 2R, and DeLaN inverse dynamics on 2R. Footer 2.
notes.1747: Introduction lists imperfect mass/inertia/friction, backlash, flexibility/compliance/contact, difficult soft/legged/deformable systems; networks approximate forward/inverse/friction/residuals and may adapt. Classical dynamics does not inherently require perfect known parameters, and learned adaptation is conditional, not automatic. Footer 3.
notes.1748: Full equation M(Θ)Θddot+C(Θ,Θdot)+G(Θ)=τ. C is the Coriolis/centrifugal generalized-force vector in this notation, not an unmultiplied n×n matrix. All position/velocity/acceleration/M/C/G/τ definitions inspected. Inverse map takes positions, velocities and accelerations to torque; feedforward/computed torque/tracking applications. No explicit friction/contact term in the displayed nominal equation. Footer 4.
notes.1749: Forward dynamics input (Θ,Θdot,τ), output acceleration, Θddot=M inverse(τ−C−G). Applications simulation, RL, MPC, digital twins. Motion requires integration after instantaneous acceleration; invertibility/model scope declared. Footer 5.
notes.1750: Three FFNN motivations: universal approximation, data-driven without exact inertial/friction equations, differentiability for optimization/autodiff/physics. Box names Deep Lagrangian, Hamiltonian and Physics-Informed networks. Approximation capacity is not a training/extrapolation guarantee; ReLU is piecewise differentiable and later higher derivatives need care. Footer 6.
notes.1751: Forward 2R diagram: six inputs θ1 θ2 θdot1 θdot2 τ1 τ2, two illustrative 32-neuron hidden layers, ReLU/tanh labels, two acceleration outputs. Arm diagram θ1 relative horizontal, θ2 relative first-link extension, lengths l1/l2 and masses m1 at elbow,m2 distal; torques τ1/τ2. Footer 7.
notes.1752: Phase1 diagram: neural identifier MLP6–30–20–2, sigmoid and standard backprop; nominal dynamics dataset deliberately spans beyond operational region, parameters differ from real inertia/friction. Broad nominal pretraining to reported1.5millioniterations and averageerror<5%. Reported benchmark not reproduced and no universal stopping guarantee; labels true accelerations are nominal-model labels, not measurements. Synthetic exploration beyond operation is not permission to drive physical robot beyond limits. Footer 8.
notes.1753: Phase2 diagram: random sinusoidal torques are bounded by actuator limits; frequencies are below half the joint natural frequencies (≤5 Hz in this example). It reports58000 responses at5 ms intervals inside the physical operating region. Fine-tuning uses the pretrained model for a reported100 iterations to an average error below5% and a plateau. Validation uses novel torques, ODE integration and comparison with real motion. The5 ms interval is200 Hz;58000 contiguous samples span289.995 s from first to last, whereas NΔt is290 s. These are source-specific conditions, not a general physical safety guarantee. Footer9.
notes.1754: The2R inverse-dynamics example has l1=l2=1 m, m1=m2=1 kg as point masses at the link tips, and g=9.81 m/s². MLP regression takes joint positions, velocities and accelerations to two torques. The figure measures θ1 from horizontal and θ2 from the first-link extension. Its input box interleaves joint triples, unlike the later grouped code order. The learned predictor need not expose parameters at inference, but synthetic label generation uses known parameters. Footer10.
notes.1755: The printed mass matrix has M11=(m1+m2)l1²+m2l2²+2m1l1l2cosθ2, M12=M21=m2l2²+m2l1l2cosθ2, and M22=m2l2². The cross term in M11 prints m1, but the illustrated distal point-mass model requires m2. Equal example masses mask the discrepancy. The full geometry and all equations were read. Footer11.
notes.1756: The slide defines h=m2l1l2sinθ2, C1=−h θdot2²−2h θdot1θdot2 and C2=h θdot1². Gravity entries are g1=(m1+m2)g l1cosθ1+m2g l2cos(θ1+θ2) and g2=m2g l2cos(θ1+θ2). Both torque row expansions include inertia, velocity-product and gravity terms. Cosine gravity matches the horizontal angle reference. C is already a force vector, so it is not multiplied by velocity again. Footer12.
notes.1757: Dataset order is X=[θ1,θ2,θdot1,θdot2,θddot1,θddot2], y=[τ1,τ2]. It differs from the earlier interleaved display but matches later code. Angles span±π, velocities±2π and accelerations±10; N=50000. Uniform joint-coordinate sampling is not uniform Cartesian workspace sampling. Independent random state tuples are not a dynamically integrated trajectory. Footer13.
notes.1758: All imports and the complete vectorized inverse_dynamics function were read. Code M11 uses2*m2*L1*L2*cos(q2), contrasting the m1 in the equation slide. The symmetric off-diagonal, h, C, gravity and torque rows match the physical point-mass model. Parameters are all unit masses/lengths with g_acc=9.81. The function generates synthetic labels, not the learned model’s prediction. Footer14.
notes.1759: Six independent np.random.uniform calls have no displayed NumPy seed. column_stack gives X shape50000×6 and Y shape50000×2. train_test_split with test_size=0.1 and random_state=42 produces45000 training and5000 test rows. The split seed does not seed earlier data generation. Random uniform draws are not guaranteed equally spaced. Footer15.
notes.1760: Pipeline combines StandardScaler and MLPRegressor with hidden widths256,256,128, tanh, max_iter500, learning_rate_init0.001, random_state42 and verboseTrue. The scaler is fitted to training inputs inside the pipeline, not targets or held-out rows. max_iter is a maximum epoch count for the default stochastic optimizer, not a guarantee of exactly500 updates. Zero-variance features qualify the unit-variance summary. Footer16.
notes.1761: Code computes per-joint sqrt(mean(square(error))) over5000 test states. Reported RMSE values are0.6311 and0.3734 N·m. The adjacent graphic omits the mean, showing a per-sample absolute error instead. A plain MLP does not structurally guarantee a positive-definite mass matrix. Footer17.
notes.1762: Both time plots were read: blue solid true torque and red dashed prediction, shoulder above and elbow below, time0 to about12.6 s. Small nonzero deviations are visible. Exact trajectory generation is not supplied on this page. The course notebook URL is visible but was not retrieved. These plots do not establish a uniform error bound or closed-loop stability. Footer18.
notes.1763: Configuration-only subnetworks output a symmetric positive-definite H(q) and potential V(q), then Euler–Lagrange relations produce torque. The last only-q-input claim is valid for subnetworks, not the complete inverse-dynamics calculation, which still needs velocity and acceleration. Footer19.
notes.1764: Torque is printed as Hddq+Hdotdq−0.5∇T+∇V, while the bottom defines T=dqᵀHdq and calls it kinetic energy. The torque expression is consistent with this doubled-energy definition, but physical kinetic energy is K=0.5dqᵀHdq and then the subtraction is −∇K. H and V alone describe the stated conservative model, not arbitrary friction or contact forces. Footer20.
notes.1765: The complete blue H path, green V path, autodiff arrows and summation were inspected. This page defines kinetic T=0.5dqᵀHdq but still subtracts0.5∇T in the velocity-product component, creating a factor-of-two defect. The position-only input graphic omits velocity and acceleration supplied to the physical computation. V contributes its gradient to gravity. Footer21.
notes.1766: The same2R model is used for a physics-structured PyTorch implementation rather than the scikit-learn black-box MLP. Only subnetworks use q alone. The5000-versus50000 dataset example is presented as data efficiency, but is not a universal tenfold guarantee or controlled comparison by itself. Footer22.
notes.1767: PyTorch, nn, NumPy, Matplotlib and Adam imports and the complete analytical label generator were inspected. The M11 cross coefficient is m2. Adam is expanded as Adaptive Moment Estimation. The label generator is distinct from the learned subnetworks. Footer23.
notes.1768: The5000 generated samples become Q,DQ,DDQ,TAU tensors of shape5000×2 and dtype float32. Aligned sequential slices at n_tr=int(0.9*N) produce4500 training and500 test samples. This is not the earlier train_test_split operation. No NumPy or PyTorch seed is displayed. Footer24.
notes.1769: Full training excerpt inspected: DeLaN2R(hidden_size=64,n_layers=2), Adam lr=0.001 and weight_decay=0.0001, MSELoss, 500 epochs, batch size128, n_batches=max(1,4500//128)=35. A new permutation is made each epoch; 4480 examples are used and20 are omitted per epoch, not necessarily the same20. zero_grad precedes backward and optimizer.step. The DeLaN2R class definition is absent from the entire lecture, so the excerpt is not standalone executable. Footer25.
notes.1770: Training-loss plot has logarithmic MSE vertical axis and epochs0–500. Large initial decrease, slower later decline and nonmonotonic spikes are visible. Training loss alone is not held-out accuracy or a guaranteed generalization bound. Footer26.
notes.1771: Prediction calls model.eval, enables autograd inside the forward calculation, then detaches the returned torque. eval is not a replacement for gradient mode and does not perform evaluation by itself. Per-joint test RMSE code is correct. Reported0.2826Nm and0.1895Nm are lower than the earlier reported MLP values, with5000versus50000generated samples; no controlled-run universal advantage is proven. Footer27.
notes.1772: All sinusoidal test code inspected:300endpoint-inclusive samples0 to4π; q1=sin(t),q2=.5sin(2t),dq1=cos(t),dq2=cos(2t),ddq1=−sin(t),ddq2=−2sin(2t). Analytical labels use the same inverse dynamics; Q_tr_/DQ_tr_/DDQ_tr_ are new300×2 float32 trajectory tensors, not training tensors despite names. predict(...).numpy assumes the detached result is on CPU. Footer28.
notes.1773: Two full sinusoidal torque plots inspected: blue true and red dashed DeLaN shoulder above/elbow below, close but not identically equal. Exact reproduction needs the omitted class and trained weights. Course notebook link is visible but no retrieval attempted. Footer29.
notes.1774: Summary introduces RNEA and ABA names, parameter/rigid-body assumptions, learned models and physics structure. Forward shorthand τ→acceleration omits conditioning on current q,dq. Energy conservation requires unforced conservative assumptions; for applied torque the proper statement is power balance, and dissipation needs additional terms. Improved generalization and future foundation/self-updating models are prospects, not unconditional guarantees. Footer30.
notes.1775: Three references only: Craig2005, Lutter/Ritter/Peters DeLaN ICLR2019, and Fang/Dissanayake forward-dynamics ICRA1998. Footer31.
